# Results on one page

**System.** A Java 21 / Spring Boot service streams NASA C-MAPSS FD001 readings (a simulated turbofan benchmark)
through Kafka. It keeps a sliding window per engine, scores remaining useful life with an in-process ONNX model and
raises de-duplicated alerts.

**Pre-registered question.** Do the 8 sensors ranked highest by correlation with RUL predict as well as all 21?
Non-inferiority margin 1.0 cycle of test RMSE, 3 seeds, 15 held-out engines.

| | Test RMSE (cycles) |
| --- | --- |
| trivial baseline | 41.58 |
| ridge, 21 sensors | 18.78 |
| gradient boosting, 21 sensors (shipped) | 12.99 ± 0.07 |
| gradient boosting, 15 informative sensors | 12.99 ± 0.07 |
| gradient boosting, 8 ranked sensors | 15.56 ± 0.06 |

**Verdict: rejected.** The gap is 2.57 cycles, above the margin. The service ships all 21 sensors.

**Post hoc** (designed after the result, labelled as such):

* Which 8 matters. Forward selection on validation: +0.89. Lowest-ranked 8: +0.97.
  Random 8: +0.83 to +2.60. The ranked 8 are redundant (mean correlation
  0.97).
* The recipe is as large as the effect. The window length moves the 21-sensor error by 1.83
  cycles; the sensor gap is 1.22 / 2.57 / 1.75 at windows of 10 / 30 / 60 readings.
* A leaky row-level split would have reported 10.08 cycles, 22% too optimistic.

**Service checks.**

* Held-out engines replayed to failure: 15/15 give exactly one
  WARNING, then one CRITICAL. CRITICAL opens 31.7 cycles before failure on average.
* Processor killed mid-stream: 20631/20631 readings scored once. Scores and alerts are identical to an uninterrupted run.
* Java and Python predictions agree on 300 real rows; 69.5 µs per prediction.
* 58 Java and 16 Python tests pass. Line coverage of the processing and alert code is 92.1%.
* 4550 ± 516 readings per second at p95 21.9 ms on a laptop (k6, 3 repeats).

**Errors.** 7.8% of test rows get a wrong status, always a neighbouring one. Of 35
inspected by hand: 3 ambiguous, 0 mislabeled, 32 model errors (lagging on
fast-failing engines, early on long-lived ones, jitter, plateaus).

**Verified in CI.** The Java suite runs on Testcontainers and `docker compose up` passes its health check in GitHub Actions.

**Not verified.** No cloud deployment, so there is no live link. All performance numbers come from one laptop.
